title: Grateful Dead Live at Wembley Empire Pool on 1972-04-08
lineage: Panasonic SV-3700 > M-Audio 2496 > Wavelab 5.0 (L3 multimaximizer, crossfades) > CD WAVE > FLAC

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording captures a stellar show highlighted by a stunning Dark Star and soaring Sugar Magnolia.
ai_review.review: The performance is praised as one of the most moving ever heard, with Dark Star flowing into an ecstatic Sugar Magnolia and a hard‑stopping Sunshine Daydream before diving back into a focused Caution jam. The encore One More Saturday Night caps the night with high energy, and the soundboard source delivers clear, balanced audio.

ai_rating.rationale: Single detailed five‑star review lauds both the musical performance and implies a clean soundboard capture; limited data set keeps confidence low.

recording_quality.technical_notes: No specific issues noted; reviewers assume clear, balanced mix typical of soundboard sources.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows organically from a soaring Dark Star into Sugar Magnolia, then transitions into Sunshine Daydream before launching into an attentive Caution jam; the encore delivers high‑energy One More Saturday Night.

band_member_comments.Bob: Bob's vocal range is described as a little narrow, suggesting his vocals were less expansive than usual.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith (Godchaux) can be heard under the jam, adding subtle keyboard texture.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey "Pig" Hart breaks out the harp and sits prominently in the mix during the jams.
